scope: Theorem 2.1 (Multiscale selector estimate) of the manuscript “Integral and fractional expectation thresholds are equivalent” (preprints/Integral-and-fractional-expectation-thresholds-are-equivalent-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 175 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0c02b128253cb6e0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X be a finite set, let F be a nonempty family of nonempty subsets of X, and suppose that F is not p-small, where 0 < p ≤ 1. For each H ∈ F, let λH be a probability mass function on X supported on H. Set D = 256, and let s ≥ 0 be an integer such that p s X i=1 Di ≤ 1 2 . Independently color the elements of X by a map a : X → {1, . . . , s + 1}, with color probabilities πi = Di p (1 ≤ i ≤ s), πs+1 = 1 − p s X i=1 Di . (2.1) For a coloring v, write Ai(v) = {x ∈ X : v(x) ≤ i}. With probability at least 9/10, there is an H ∈ F such that λH(Ai(a)) ≥ 1 − 2−i (1 ≤ i ≤ s). (2.2) In particular, with probability at least 9/10, there is an H ∈ F for which X x∈X a(x)λH(x) ≤ 2. (2.3)
